title: MemoryRecord
description: One durable fact in the project memory store. Provenance is not bookkeeping — it is what makes a contradictory memory resolvable and a bad memory revocable. A run may propose a record; only a verified outcome promotes it, which is what stops the store filling with the confident assertions of runs that turned out to be wrong.

category.description: Drives TTL, invalidation triggers, and who is permitted to write it.

scope.description: What this record is about. Used to invalidate on change and to scope retrieval.

tenant_id.description: Memory is never shared across tenants.

evidence.description: Verdict ids, file:line, test names. A record with no evidence may be stored but stays unverified.

verified.description: True only when a passing gate outcome backs it. Unverified records are retrievable but labelled inline so the agent weighs them as hypotheses, not facts.

source_trust.description: Content originating from issue text, web pages, PR comments, or third-party tool output is untrusted and must never be promoted to a verified fact on its own.

ttl_days.description: Null for semantic and procedural records. Operational ≈ 90, episodic detail ≈ 180.

supersedes.description: Set when this record resolves a contradiction. Contradictions are flagged and resolved by provenance strength and recency — never silently overwritten.

invalidated_by.description: Merge, contract change, superseding ADR, or verified fix that made this record false. Invalidated records leave the retrieval index immediately — a stale contract is worse than no contract.

versions.description: Append-only mutation history so a bad or leaked entry can be redacted and its blast radius traced.
